cleanup.agent_browser_cleanup: After the test browser exited, close tried to reconnect to the dead CDP endpoint. The current named-session info identified its empty daemon PID 44036; that owned daemon was terminated and session-list confirmed absence.

diagnostics: The first native query executed New Tab because NSMenu adopted the system interface style and replaced the query-aware root view. The shared provider now preserves style and restores its hooks after the native setMain implementation; both the native visible-root query assertion and Chromium query/cancellation cases pass.

Early checker cleanup used Ctrl+W and then Ctrl+F4 while the native address editor was focused. Their editor handling left the test-created tab open. Cleanup now uses the observed tab close button and waits through Chromium insertion animation; page focus selects the original tab physically before DOM focus.

A native button can execute its actual application menu inside existing native control dispatch, so that case witnesses one provider command and actual engine execution rather than requiring a second BrowserView unhandled hook.

The original Chromium clipboard test required field-filter provenance. With a native application menu, GNUstep correctly handles the shortcut through that menu. A temporary editor-menu-first experiment was removed: the final provider preserves existing native application-menu-first ordering. The opt-in checker instead requires validation plus exactly one actual application-menu execution, while retaining all clipboard event, cancellation and editing checks.
The first Firefox regression launcher omitted the private Chromium dependency directory containing libatk and exited before XPCOM initialization. It was corrected in subsequent owned fixtures.

An application-menu clipboard checker was also invoked against the Workspace-owned control descriptor, whose fixture intentionally does not accept manual menu-broker commands. Global checks run against Workspace association; field clipboard checks run against the supported explicit fixture binding.
Clang-only guard compilation produces the identical Chromium adapter hash as the tested candidate. GCC is explicitly rejected rather than silently ignoring the existing naked wrapper.
remaining: Chromium global native menu command-boundary integration and Chrome/Vivaldi/Firefox derivative qualification.
Standard session shared-host startup/packaging, private role supervision and production registrar/bus recovery.
Broader keyboard/reservation policy, special keys and multi-chord metadata, remaining browser controls/dialogs, IME, accessibility and scaling.
Complete GTK, Qt/KDE and other non-GNUstep application coverage.
Qualify additional Chromium/Chrome/Vivaldi and Firefox derivative builds; current instruction guards cover the recorded Chromium and Firefox executables only.
Complete native controls across browser frontend and web content, including existing documented pointer, IME, accessibility and scaling gaps, then complete non-GNUstep toolkit integration.
Install and qualify the shared helper, launch policy and shell association in the ordinary desktop session; isolated fixtures are not system-wide deployment.
